title: Terminal session split into identity (TerminalSource) and bytes (TerminalTransport)
context: A terminal session has two separate concerns: which terminals exist, their names, and which window's panel holds one (shared state); versus which PTY's output goes where and the emulator's keystrokes back (per-session, high-volume).
decision: Create two separate interfaces: TerminalSource for identity/lifetime (Rust-owned, projected from shell:state), and TerminalTransport for bytes (one per session, per-emulator).
consequences: Allows a single interception point at the transport seam in Rust. Enables tracking what a coding harness did and injecting input without cooperation from every component.
